I will keep my farm arranged around the wheat-maize system first, because that is the most reliable way for me to keep grain coming from my land and make full use of the year. Since I only have 8 mu and some people in my family work off-farm, I will not make the plan too complicated. I will put 4 mu into the wheat-maize rotation, so that same 4 mu grows winter wheat first and then summer maize after harvest. On the other 4 mu, I will split the land between cotton and mungbean. I will keep 2 mu of cotton because it brings cash, but it needs more spraying and labor, so I will not expand it too much. I will keep 2 mu of mungbean because it is lighter to manage, fits well in summer, and helps spread my risk if one crop does poorly. I have well irrigation, so I will use water at the key times instead of depending only on rain. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters most, put more fertilizer on wheat, maize, and cotton, and keep mungbean inputs lower. I will also choose tillage that saves time in the busy wheat-maize turnover period, because I know the summer changeover is tight and I cannot afford delays.
